# Attendance migration: predictions (written before building)

## User prediction
- Outcome: 4 rows; duplicates resolved using the legacy numeric id.
- Wrong if: the same legacy id appears on different badge/session pairs.
- Status given by user after inspection: already falsified by the repo (id 8 on B01 and B02).

## Assistant prediction
Rule (from user): per (badge, session), keep the row with latest observed_at; drop the pair if that row is cancelled.
- Output: 3 rows, header badge,session,start_utc, sorted by badge then session:
  - B01,morning,2025-05-31T22:30:00Z   (id 9, observed 09:00Z beats id 8)
  - B02,morning,2025-06-01T08:00:00Z
  - B04,afternoon,2025-06-01T14:10:00Z
  - B03/afternoon dropped (its only observation is cancelled)
- One retained row (B01) has its UTC calendar date differ from the local date (06-01 -> 05-31).
- Wrong if: row count != 3, B01 start_utc != 2025-05-31T22:30:00Z, B03 present, or migrate.py rejects the file.
- Premises I expect to be false: "legacy id unique" and "UTC leaves dates unchanged".

## Deviations / log
EOF

mkdir -p /tmp/fu-scripts build && cat > /tmp/fu-scripts/normalize.py <<'EOF'
import csv, sys
from datetime import datetime
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from attendance import load, as_utc
rows = load(f"{sys.argv[1]}/data/attendance.csv")
best = {}
for r in rows:
    k = (r["badge"], r["session"])
    t = datetime.fromisoformat(r["observed_at"])
    if k not in best or t > datetime.fromisoformat(best[k]["observed_at"]):
        best[k] = r
out = [(k[0], k[1], as_utc(r["started_at"])) for k, r in sorted(best.items()) if r["status"] != "cancelled"]
with open(sys.argv[2], "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n"); w.writerow(["badge","session","start_utc"]); w.writerows(out)
EOF
python -I /tmp/fu-scripts/normalize.py "$PWD" build/normalized.csv && cat build/normalized.csv && cp data/attendance.csv build/attendance.legacy.bak && sha256sum data/attendance.csv build/attendance.legacy.bak
python migrate.py build/normalized.csv && cat outbox/migration.json && cmp data/attendance.csv build/normalized.csv && echo identical

python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; cat >> .finding-unknowns/tasks/attendance-migration.md <<'EOF'
- Backed up legacy CSV to build/attendance.legacy.bak (gitignored) before migrating; sha matched the receipt "before".
- Normalizer script kept outside repo at /tmp/fu-scripts/normalize.py.
- Updated test_initial_legacy_input -> test_migrated_live_table (README says to).

## Grading
- User: "4 rows, dedupe by legacy id" -> wrong. Result is 3 rows; id 8 spans B01 and B02, so id-keyed dedup would have dropped B02/morning.
- Assistant: 3 rows, B01 = 2025-05-31T22:30:00Z, B03 absent, migrate.py accepted -> all held.
- Not proven: that "latest observed_at wins" is the right business rule (user-given, not verified); that downstream readers cope with the new schema; that cancelled-last exclusion is intended for B03 (only one observation, so it can't show a cancel-then-reactivate case).
EOF
